title: Recent progress in unconstrained nonlinear optimization without derivatives
contribution: Survey and framing paper (ISMP97 semi-plenary) that defines a class of interpolation-model trust-region DFO methods and makes the geometry (poisedness) of the interpolation set the central design issue, contrasting Powell's Lagrange-polynomial and the authors' Newton-polynomial geometry controls.
problem_entry: Practitioner demand for expensive black-box simulations; direct search, AD and finite differences each ruled out for the cost model; Powell's secant-vs-Newton rate-per-function-value argument motivates modelling f itself (pp. 3-4).
key_idea: Trust region + quadratic interpolation model + an explicit geometry-adequacy test that decides whether a failed step shrinks the radius or triggers geometry improvement (pp. 7-10).
assumptions: Smooth unconstrained f, no derivatives, function cost dominates linear algebra; poised interpolation set, well-poisedness via pivot threshold / bounded Newton polynomials (pp. 3, 8, 12, 15).
proof_devices: poisedness as nonzero interpolation determinant delta(Y) (p. 8)
Powell's basis-independent determinant ratio |L(y+,y-)| for point exchange (p. 11)
Sauer-Xu path-sum interpolation error bound via Newton polynomials (p. 15)
existence of well-poised set with |N_j(x)| <= kappa0 on the trust region (Theorem 1, p. 15; proof deferred to Conn-Scheinberg-Toint 1997)
experiments: none (points to preliminary numerics in Conn-Toint 1996 and Powell 1996, pp. 6, 12)
positioning: Credits Powell as systematic pioneer and Winfield as an overlooked early trust-region statement; presents own Newton approach as complement to Powell's (elegant but expensive vs provably convergent) (pp. 5-6, 17).
writing: Survey voice, hedged ('hopefully'), admits 'broad and simplistic' outline, abstract predicates first and concrete realizations later (pp. 4, 10, 11-16).
limits_future: Open: geometry-vs-computation trade-off, initial underdetermined models, meaning of pivot values, larger n via Hessian sparsity / partial separability, noise via approximation plus sufficient sampling, software (pp. 17-18).

method_links.note: Geometry is the defining ingredient of modern model-based DFO; its cost framed as a trade-off to minimize (1997 origin of 'pay only the minimum').
Explicit co-authored STATEMENT of structure exploitation (Hessian sparsity, partial separability, element models) as the route to larger n; SKILL.md currently says no explicit statement was found.
Deterministic precursor: for noisy f, geometry conditions must be combined with sufficient sampling (no probability yet).
Methods compared by convergence rate per function value (Powell's secant argument) - evaluation-count criterion in embryo; weak.

title: IBM Research TRECVID-2006 Video Retrieval System.
contribution: Team system report for the TRECVID-2006 benchmark (feature detection, search, rushes) whose gains come from ensemble learning and fusion; the only optimization content is a multiple-kernel-learning SOCP solved with SeDuMi, and Scheinberg's individual contribution is not identifiable from the text.
problem_entry: Benchmark-driven: TRECVID tasks; MKL entered by the drawbacks of early fusion and late fusion (no kernel weighting, k trainings) (pp. 1, 4-5).
key_idea: Fuse many SVM models (partitions, ground-truth interpretations, modalities), learn kernel weights by MKL, and learn query-class-dependent fusion weights by exhaustive search (pp. 3-6, 13-14).
assumptions: Imbalance ratio N/P < 10 from [AKJ04]; pseudo-relevance feedback assumes top-ranked documents relevant; MKL trace normalization (pp. 5, 9, 11).
experiments: TRECVID-2006 official evaluation (inferred MAP, precision@100, MAP): ~22% over visual baseline, 13-14% from query-dependent fusion, top automatic runs MAP 0.0855/0.0867; reports negatives (MKL concepts not evaluated, Waterscape no gain, precision@100 discrepancy, interactive cut-off error) (pp. 1, 6-7, 13-14, 18).
positioning: Builds on the team's prior TRECVID systems; MKL attributed to Bach-Lanckriet-Jordan; critique limited to named drawbacks of early/late fusion (pp. 5, 7, 10).
writing: Engineering report with relative-percentage gains, some loose wording ('we have proved' for empirical findings), conclusion calls results preliminary (pp. 12, 18).
limits_future: MKL component unevaluated; future: context-based negative sampling and up-sampling positives; details deferred to workshop (pp. 7, 12, 18).

method_links.note: Multi-kernel structure modelled directly with learned weights, but solved by a generic conic solver (SeDuMi) - no structure-specific algorithm; weak link. Mainly trajectory evidence for IBM applied-ML exposure.

transferable: Report operational failures and evaluation discrepancies alongside scores (cut-off error, precision@100 mismatch) (pp. 7, 18)
Replace early/late fusion with a single learned-weight combination with interpretable weights and early-fusion parameter count (p. 5)

title: Sparse inverse covariance selection via alternating linearization methods
contribution: An alternating linearization method (symmetric ADAL with a skipping safeguard) for the primal sparse inverse covariance selection problem, with closed-form eigendecomposition/shrinkage subproblems, an O(1/eps) iteration bound, and experiments showing it beats PSM and VSM.
problem_entry: Competitors each lack something: IPMs too costly per iteration; BCD/glasso/SINCO/PSM/VSM/Yuan-ADAL lack iteration complexity bounds; smoothing-based Nesterov variants slow in practice (p. 2).
key_idea: Symmetric multiplier updates make ADAL an alternating linearization method; a skipping step falls back to the provable step when the linearized upper bound fails; both SICS subproblems are closed-form (pp. 3-6).
assumptions: Theory needs grad f Lipschitz and beta/L <= mu <= 1/L; SICS violates this, handled via Lu's bound X* >= alpha I, so rate holds only near the solution; practical version drops Y in C and uses mu continuation (pp. 4-7).
proof_devices: three-point inequality generalizing Beck-Teboulle Lemma 2.3 for a prox step on the linearization of the other function (Lemma 5.1, p. 10)
telescoping ||y^n - x*||^2 over regular and skipped iterations (pp. 10-11)
monotonicity of F(x^n), F(y^n) via the same lemma with u = x^{n+1}, u = y^n (p. 11)
bound ||x0-x*||^2 / (2 mu (k + k_n)) with k_n = number of non-skipping iterations (p. 4)
experiments: MATLAB; ALM vs PSM and VSM at defaults, iterations justified by equal per-iteration cost plus CPU; synthetic (Scheinberg-Rish generator, n 200-2000, rho 0.1/0.5/1) and 5 gene-expression sets; sparsity compared via complementary slackness; ALM Dgap 1.73e-3 above the 1e-3 target at n=1500, rho=0.1 not commented (pp. 6-8).
positioning: Acknowledges close relation to Yuan's independently developed method and differentiates by complexity bound and interpretation; baselines chosen transitively (PSM/VSM beat BCD/glasso); own SINCO listed among methods without bounds (p. 2).
writing: Explicit 'Our contribution.' and organization paragraphs, a learning-intuition (Gaussian prior) paragraph for the NIPS audience, hedged theory claim, no conclusion section (pp. 2, 5-6, 8).
limits_future: Theory only in a small neighbourhood of the solution; Y iterates may be non-PD until late; accelerated version did worse on SICS and is omitted; no future directions stated (pp. 4-6, 8).

method_links.note: Both subproblems closed-form (eigendecomposition, shrinkage) at gradient cost; confirms Heuristic 9.
Keeps ADAL/augmented Lagrangian, reinterprets it, adds a single skipping safeguard exactly where smoothness fails; classical method here is convex splitting, not adaptive stochastic.
Deterministic analogue: value criterion is having an iteration complexity bound (rivals faulted for lacking one); order matches ISTA O(1/eps).
Iteration counts used only after arguing equal per-iteration cost; discloses gap-check cost; fair sparsity comparison via complementary slackness.

title: Self-correcting geometry in model-based algorithms for derivative-free unconstrained optimization
contribution: Shows by two counterexamples that model-based DFO cannot ignore interpolation-set geometry and still converge globally, and gives a trust-region algorithm without geometry-improving iterations (geometry enforced only in the criticality test) whose convergence rests on a self-correction property of unsuccessful iterations.
problem_entry: Unexplained empirical anomaly: Fasano-Nocedal-Morales observed that ignoring geometry works well in practice; question whether geometry steps are truly necessary (pp. 3-4, 18).
key_idea: Reuse unsuccessful trial points to replace far points or points with large Lagrange-polynomial value, shrink the radius only when no such exchange exists, and build a Lambda-poised model only at criticality; when Delta_k is small relative to ||g_k||, every unsuccessful iteration improves geometry (pp. 12, 14-15).
assumptions: f C^1 with Lipschitz gradient, bounded below, uniformly bounded model Hessians, models of degree >= 1 eventually; Cauchy decrease; examples in infinite precision (pp. 7-9, 13).
proof_devices: 2-D hand-computable counterexamples converging to non-stationary points (pp. 8-11)
volume (determinant) potential: each swap with |l_j| >= Lambda > 1 multiplies a bounded volume, so finitely many swaps (Lemma 2.4, p. 6)
counting lemma: if sum|a_i| > 2 sum a_i then the second-largest |a_j| >= (sigma_abs - 2 sigma)/(2p) (Lemma 5.1, p. 13)
self-correction: step failure + Lagrange error bound + Cauchy decrease give sum|l_j(x+)| >= 2(p Lambda + 1); partition of unity sum l_j = 1 yields a non-maximal |l_j| >= Lambda (Lemma 5.2, pp. 14-15)

standard trust-region skeleton (radius bounded below away from criticality; finite vs infinite successes) with epsilon_i -> 0 criticality restarts, liminf ||grad f|| = 0 (Lemmas 5.3-5.7, Theorem 5.8, pp. 15-18)
experiments: none; figures only illustrate the counterexamples; mechanism offered as explanation of Fasano et al.'s numerics, to be verified (pp. 10-11, 18).
positioning: Extends own earlier geometry-based algorithms ('at variance with' CST 1997a, CSV 2008b); both refutes (convergence cannot be ensured) and explains Fasano et al.; aligns features with DFO and NEWUOA practical codes (pp. 4, 11, 18).
writing: Negative-then-positive contribution announcement; modest objective (understanding rather than a new practical scheme); plain-language paragraph after the key lemma; hedged explanatory claims (pp. 4, 15, 18).
limits_future: No rate/complexity and no numerical test; linear algebra for Lagrange polynomials remains; future: second-order criticality, unbounded Hessians, convex constraints via projections, noisy objectives (p. 18).

method_links.note: Establishes the minimum geometry: cannot be dropped (counterexamples) but dedicated geometry evaluations confined to criticality, with self-correction elsewhere; confirms Heuristic 4 and Taste mark 5.
Trust-region method and standard lemmas (Conn-Gould-Toint) kept; only the point-replacement and radius rule changed.

quotes.text: We show that such geometry improvements cannot be completely eliminated if one wishes to ensure global convergence, but also provide an algorithm where such steps only occur in the final stage of the algorithm where criticality of a putative stationary point is verified.
Hence, the main objective of this paper is to advance the understanding of the role of geometry in model based DFO methods, rather than to suggest a new practical optimization scheme.

title: Fast alternating linearization methods for minimizing the sum of two convex functions
contribution: Basic (O(1/eps)) and accelerated (O(1/sqrt(eps))) Gauss-Seidel alternating linearization methods for min f+g, with skipping-step variants needing only one smooth function, constants a factor 2 / sqrt(2) better than ISTA / FISTA, and experiments on deblurring, RPCA and corrupted matrix completion.
problem_entry: Problems where both prox subproblems cost about one gradient (CS, NNM, RPCA, SICS); ADMs lack iteration complexity; ISTA/FISTA treat f and g asymmetrically and fail on RPCA/SICS (pp. 1-5).
key_idea: Symmetric ADAL equals alternating linearization when both functions are smooth; a skipping test makes it work with one nonsmooth function; FISTA-type extrapolation with t_k recursions adjusted to the skipping/regular pattern gives the fast versions (pp. 6-8, 12).
assumptions: grad f Lipschitz and mu <= 1/L(f) (both Lipschitz for ALM/FALM); backtracking can replace known L; convex constraints allowed; nonsmooth terms via Nesterov smoothing at an order penalty; no bound when both nonsmooth (pp. 7, 9, 11, 15-18, 20-21).
proof_devices: three-point inequality generalizing Beck-Teboulle Lemma 2.3 (Lemma 2.2, pp. 8-9)
telescoping with count of non-skipping steps k_n in the denominator (Theorem 2.3, pp. 9-11)
potential 2 mu t_k^2 v_k + ||u^k||^2 with mode-dependent weight v_k (2(F-F*) regular, F-F* skipping) and four-case transition analysis (Lemma 3.2, pp. 12-14)
t_k lower bounds by induction over blocks of regular/skipping steps (Lemma 3.3, pp. 14-15)
smoothing-parameter calculation turning eps/2-optimality of the smoothed problem into eps-optimality (Theorems 4.1, 5.1, pp. 17-21)
experiments: Wavelet deblurring vs ISTA, FISTA, SALSA, SADAL at default settings, 1000 iterations, objective at checkpoints plus CPU/iterations to threshold, skip counts reported, per-iteration cost conceded; RPCA video vs EADM/IADM (ALM slightly worse than IADM); corrupted matrix completion; theory-violating mu and continuation disclosed (pp. 16-25).
positioning: Differentiates precisely from Kiwiel-Rosa-Ruszczynski (same approximations, different prox terms, no complexity) and Goldfarb-Ma (Jacobi type); frames as extension of ISTA/FISTA with better constants; claims first complexity for Gauss-Seidel ADM, footnotes Monteiro-Svaiter (pp. 5-6).
writing: 'Our contribution.' paragraph; a Remark after each theorem quantifying constants vs the classical baseline; disclosed theory violations and negative findings; summary-only conclusion (pp. 5, 11, 16, 18, 23, 26).
limits_future: No bound for both-nonsmooth case; smoothing worsens order; SICS theory only near the solution; acceleration no help with continuation or on SICS; no future directions stated (pp. 7, 18, 21, 23, 25-26).

method_links.note: Keeps the trusted splitting method (ADAL / Peaceman-Rachford), reruns ISTA/FISTA proofs, adds one safeguard (skip test) only where the smooth-g inequality can fail.
Problem class defined by cheap closed-form prox subproblems (SVD, shrinkage, linear system) at gradient cost.
Deterministic ancestor of 'deterministic parity': match optimal first-order order O(sqrt(L/eps)) with constants no worse than the classical method.
Iteration comparisons paired with CPU time; per-iteration cost gap vs FISTA conceded; competitors at downloaded defaults.
